HEAD:docs/ASTRA_REVIEW_7160.md:14:This is not approval for automatic legacy recovery or exposing `rebind_plan_owner` to untrusted callers. Rebind is a trusted in-process authority override, not authentication of lost history: it can assign a quarantined plan to an unrelated unlinked incident, and held post-migration plan-only successes can then close that incident. Its caller must supply the missing authority. There is no production caller/integration in this pin. The remaining late-INCIDENT liveness defect, diagnostic retention growth, and multi-plan supersession contract deserve fixes, but the tested current-format live paths did not produce unsafe success.
HEAD:docs/ASTRA_REVIEW_7160.md:119:`rebind-authority.json` demonstrates the exact abuse boundary with authentic old producer: historical PLAN p->historical loses its owner; two **fresh post-migration plan-only successes** are held; explicit `rebind_plan_owner('p','unrelated')` closes unrelated and leaves historical open. Without those fresh successes, both stay open. Twenty current restores retain one audit entry without multiplication.
HEAD:docs/ASTRA_REVIEW_7173.md:116:Candidates are recorded by ordinary PLAN events, not authenticated ownership evidence. `allow_non_candidate=True` remains a deliberate trust override. Findings 2 and 3 delimit what the positive preview tests do not establish.

HEAD:README.md:86:## Hive rebind journal
HEAD:README.md:88:Operator rebinds of held plans are made durable by a write-ahead journal:
HEAD:README.md:91:export HIVE_REBIND_JOURNAL=$(pwd)/state/hive-rebinds.jsonl
HEAD:README.md:94:Without a journal, `HiveAppliance` refuses rebinds unless you pass
HEAD:README.md:95:`volatile_rebinds=True`. Each rebind is journaled as a pending record plus a
HEAD:README.md:96:commit record, and only committed rebinds replay. Each journal starts with a
HEAD:README.md:97:header carrying a random id, also stored in `<journal>.id`; a mismatch (an old
HEAD:README.md:98:journal swapped back) fences it. `rebind_plan_owner()` returns a `RebindResult`
HEAD:README.md:99:(`applied` / `refused` / `uncertain`; only `applied` is truthy). If any journal record cannot
HEAD:README.md:100:be verified (torn, edited, reordered, legacy v1-v4 format), the whole journal is
HEAD:README.md:101:fenced: `journal_status()["healthy"]` is False, nothing is replayed and rebinds
HEAD:README.md:103:`clear_journal_fence(actor=..., reason=...)`, which archives the old journal
HEAD:README.md:104:and starts a new one; re-issue any rebind still wanted. See
HEAD:README.md:105:`docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md` ("Hive rebind journal").

HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:91:  `rebind_pending` record, then, once that is durable, a `rebind_commit`
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:92:  record naming it (`op_id` plus the pending record's hash). Only rebinds
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:94:  rebind was refused, or the process stopped between the two writes) is
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:97:- **Journal identity (Astra 7694).** The first record of every journal is a
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:98:  `journal_header` carrying a random `journal_id`; the hash chain starts
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:99:  from it. The current `journal_id` is also stored, fsync'd, in a separate
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:100:  identity anchor file `<journal>.id`. If the journal's header does not match
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:101:  the anchor (an older or archived journal -- even a valid one -- was put back
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:103:  a journal that has been removed, the whole journal is fenced
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:104:  (`fence.kind == "identity"`). Keep `<journal>.id` next to the journal and
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:105:  back up / restore the two together. A header-only journal without an anchor
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:106:  (crash between creating the two) is adopted, since it holds no rebinds.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:111:  accidental and naive edits; they are NOT a keyed MAC (someone with write
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:112:  access who recomputes every hash is not detected), so protect the journal
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:114:- **Fail closed on the whole journal.** At startup, if ANY record cannot be
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:118:  record missing only its final newline -- NO journaled rebind is replayed.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:119:  The journal is reported unhealthy (`journal_status()["healthy"]` False,
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:120:  `fence` says why, `corrupt_records` gives the line) and every new rebind is
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:121:  refused. The journal is never trimmed or repaired, so it fences again after
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:123:  `<journal>.fence` file also fences everything.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:124:- **Result of `rebind_plan_owner()` (Astra 7694).** A `RebindResult`:
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:125:  `status` is `"applied"` (truthy; with a journal, its commit record is
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:127:  commit durability unknown, journal fenced; after a restart it is replayed or
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:130:  as `last_rebind_result`.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:133:  - Pending write fails, rollback OK: clean refusal, journal stays healthy.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:134:  - Pending write fails AND rollback fails: refused and fenced (unhealthy).
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:136:    never replay; a torn tail fences the journal at the next start.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:137:  - Commit write fails, rollback OK: clean refusal; the pending record stays
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:138:    on disk without a commit and never replays. Journal stays healthy.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:139:  - Commit write fails AND rollback fails: the commit may or may not be
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:141:    rebind is applied in memory and `rebind_plan_owner()` returns an explicit
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:142:    `RebindResult` with `status == "uncertain"` (`applied=True`,
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:143:    `durable=None`, falsy), and the journal is fenced
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:146:    lost) or the whole journal is fenced (commit torn) -- never a refused
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:147:    rebind coming back.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:148:  - Before every write the identity anchor must still name this journal and
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:149:    the journal must be byte-for-byte what this process last wrote or
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:151:    `verify_journal()` runs the same check on demand. Between writes nothing
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:153:    `verify_journal()` call or restart. Otherwise (changed, truncated,
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:154:    removed or torn from outside) nothing is written and the journal is
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:156:  - A journal that cannot be created or read at startup is fenced
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:157:    (`unwritable`): the process reports unhealthy and refuses rebinds.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:158:- **Clearing a fence.** Inspect the journal, then call
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:159:  `clear_journal_fence(actor=..., reason=...)`. It copies the old journal
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:160:  byte-for-byte to `<journal>.fenced-<ns>` (fsync'd, directory fsync'd),
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:161:  then atomically replaces the journal with a new one (new random
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:162:  `journal_id` in a fresh `journal_header`, then the anchor is replaced) that
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:163:  continues with a `journal_reset` record (actor, reason, archive path) and re-journals, as
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:164:  pending + commit pairs, exactly the rebinds this process holds applied or
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:166:  state. Rebinds in the old journal that were not applied are NOT carried
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:167:  over: re-issue them if still wanted. Any failure raises and the journal
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:169:  `journal_status()["fence_clearances"]`.
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:170:- **Upgrading (behaviour change).** v1-v4 journals are legacy format and
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:171:  fence the whole journal at the first start after upgrading: nothing in them
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:172:  is replayed. Review the journal, clear the fence, and re-issue each rebind
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:173:  that is still wanted with `rebind_plan_owner()`.

HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:178:  its incident stays OPEN, counted in `plans_refused_cap`). `journal_status()`
HEAD:docs/POLICY_MULTI_PLAN_SUPERSESSION.md:180:  `unapplied_omitted`. `journal_unapplied()` returns all retained dispositions
